subject: S3-backed vector snapshot sync: certification & retention pilot
messages:
From: Alex Turner <alex@pinecone.io>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel@redwoodai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwoodai.com>
Date: Tue, 02 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot: S3-backed vector snapshot sync (prototype & data retention ask)

Hi Rachel,

Thanks again for the call last week. As discussed, we put together a lightweight proposal for a joint pilot that demonstrates Pinecone acting as a lightweight index fronting S3 snapshots for cost-optimized cold lane retrieval. High-level goals:

- Validate snapshot export/import flow from Redwood Dedicated -> S3 -> Pinecone ingestion.
- Verify prefix-level retention/TTL semantics and pedigree mapping for compliance audits.
- Measure cold-read P99 and per-query egress unit economics for mixed workloads.

Attached are: snapshot_schema_v1.yaml (schema we propose for object keys + metadata), and a simple retention-matrix.xlsx that maps retention policies to Pinecone collection lifecycle events.

Ask from our side: can Redwood provide a small test dataset (up to 50k vectors, with metadata including customer_id and created_at) and a short-lived S3 bucket with signed access for the pilot? We can stand up a Pinecone sandbox collection and a small ingestion lambda that pulls objects and indexes them.

Operational notes:
- We can host the ingestion in our sandbox region (us-west-2) and provide a read-only service account.
- For SLA/retention proofs, Samira (cc'ed) from our partner team will help gather documentation.

If this looks good, we can aim to start a two-week tech pilot the week of 4/16. Next steps:
1) Redwood confirms dataset and S3 access model.
2) We share a sandbox ingestion runbook + IAM snippet.
3) Quick sync to align retention semantics and audit logs.

Best,
Alex Turner
Partner Solutions, Pinecone

---
Attachments: snapshot_schema_v1.yaml (text), retention-matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Rachel Kim <rachel@redwoodai.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex@pinecone.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwoodai.com>, Irene Choi <irene@redwoodai.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwoodai.com>
Date: Wed, 03 Apr 2028 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot: S3-backed vector snapshot sync (prototype & data retention ask)

Alex — thanks for the clear plan and the assets. This aligns with what our GTM/partner track expects. A few notes from Redwood's side before we lock dates: 

1) Dataset: we can provide a 30k-vector extract from our non-prod replay cluster. We will strip PII and include only customer_id-level identifiers (no emails). Delivery model: a short-lived S3 bucket with presigned PUTs (48h lifetime).

2) Retention/audit: Irene (cc) will own the retention mapping and needs to confirm that Pinecone can persist a stable audit id per object in your collection metadata so we can reconcile on restore. The retention-matrix looks like a good starting point — please highlight where Pinecone expects TTL enforcement vs. us managing object lifecycle in S3.

3) Security/compliance: Vanessa will coordinate minimal evidence for the pilot (SOC2 snapshot of sandbox controls, encryption at rest notes). We need to ensure the ingestion process writes an ingestion log (S3 object with manifest) that we can include in an audit.

4) Timeline: 2-week pilot starting 2028-04-16 is fine. Before that we need: signed partner NDA addendum (low friction), an IAM snippet for a read-only ingestion principal, and a simple failure/retry runbook.

Action items:
- Alex: send IAM snippet + sandbox ingestion runbook by EOD Thu 4/4.
- Ben: small internal kickoff to allocate infra hours for extraction — Ben will confirm.
- Irene: will draft retention reconciliation questions and send back by 4/6.
- Vanessa: will list required compliance artifacts and target delivery date.

If you want to run a quick 30-minute sync tomorrow to walk the team through the runbook, I'm available 10:00–11:30 PDT.

Thanks,
Rachel Kim
Strategic Partnerships, Redwood Inference

Folks — forwarding the Pinecone proposal and Rachel's response. Quick notes from infra planning: 

- I can carve out a non-prod snapshot pipeline and produce the 30k-vector export by next Tues (4/9). Will need a 2-hour window for exporting and one for validation.
- Prefer using a temporary S3 bucket under our partner account with presigned PUTs as Rachel suggested. That keeps lifecycle controls simple.
- We should include a checksum step in the manifest to make reconciliation straightforward for Irene.

Proposed internal checklist before we hand to Pinecone:
- Export manifest with object-level checksums + created_at
- Tag objects with redwood:pilot=true and customer_bucket_tag set to pseudo-customer ids
- Provide a read-only IAM role with a narrow prefix (no wildcard) and a KMS key policy that allows Pinecone ingest principal only for this object prefix

Irene — can you confirm retention reconciliation fields you need (e.g., ingestion_id, original_object_key, last_modified, created_at)? I can ensure the manifest includes them.

Ben
Senior Eng, Indexing & Integrations

Thanks all — good progress. Short update and attachments we just added: an integration diagram (s3-integration-diagram.png) and a brief sandbox runbook (link in Drive).

Responses to asks:
- IAM snippet: see below (we'll provide the least-privilege role reading only prefix/* and ListBucket for the pilot).
- TTL vs retention: Pinecone will maintain collection-level metadata and can persist an ingestion_id per vector as requested. TTL enforcement (automatic deletion) is supported at collection level but for compliance purposes we recommend you retain authoritative copies in S3 and use Pinecone TTL as a convenience layer — we'll highlight where lifecycle events fire in our logs so your ingestion manifest can reconcile.
- Audit trace: We'll produce an ingestion manifest on our side that maps ingestion_id -> original_object_key and provide a signed artifact after each ingestion run.

Sandbox link: https://app.pinecone.io/sandbox/teams/redwood/collections/vec-sync (read-only for Redwood test principal)
DocuSign request: DOCUSIGN-REQ-55321 (NDA addendum to enable pilot)

Next steps:
- Samira will coordinate the small SOC2/sandbox controls packet by 4/7.
- Rachel/Ben: confirm export window (Ben noted 4/9) and share the S3 prefix + KMS arn when ready.
- We'll schedule the 30-minute runbook walkthru on Mon 4/9 10:00 PDT — calendar invite to follow.

Appreciate the fast turnaround — excited to get this running.

Best,
Alex Turner
Partner Solutions, Pinecone
